title: Giant's Chess Match Over Tokyo
description: A surreal city simulation where a giant chess set from ABeautifulGame hovers above the LittlestTokyo cityscape. The user plays as a cosmic entity who can pick up chess pieces and drop them onto the city, triggering localized physics-based shockwaves that ripple through nearby buildings. The goal is to place all major pieces onto designated landing zones scattered across the city within a time limit while keeping structural damage below a threshold.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with es module shims) that loads both LittlestTokyo.glb and ABeautifulGame.glb via GLTFLoader and DRACOLoader (decoder path https://www.gstatic.com/draco/v1/decoders/). Place LittlestTokyo at the origin scaled to fill the scene as a city base. Extract individual chess pieces from ABeautifulGame by traversing its scene graph, separate the 6 major white pieces (king, queen, 2 rooks, 2 bishops), scale them up 15x, and position them floating 80 units above the city in a row. Add a semi-transparent green grid overlay on the city marking 6 circular landing zones at distinct positions. Implement OrbitControls for camera navigation with initial perspective looking down at 45 degrees. Use a hemisphere light plus a directional light with shadow mapping enabled. Create a raycaster-based drag interaction: on pointerdown, raycast to detect chess pieces; on pointermove, move the selected piece along a horizontal plane at its current Y; on pointerup near a landing zone, animate the piece dropping with a TWEEN-style lerp to the zone center at ground level. On landing, trigger a shockwave: create an expanding transparent ring at impact, and for all LittlestTokyo child meshes within radius 20, apply a brief oscillating rotation animation simulating structural shake. Track a damage meter (0-100%) displayed as an HTML overlay bar; each drop adds 5-15% damage based on piece weight (queen=15, king=12, rook=10, bishop=8). Display a 120-second countdown timer. Show piece count placed (e.g. 2/6). Add parameter validation: pieces must land within 5 units of a zone center to count, pieces cannot be placed on already-occupied zones, and the simulation fails if damage exceeds 80%. When all 6 pieces are placed or time expires, show a results overlay with pieces placed, damage percentage, and time remaining. Play LittlestTokyo animations via AnimationMixer throughout.
